subject.title: [优化建议] install.sh 模块化拆分以提升可维护性

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a modular `scripts/install.sh` source layout now, and if so should the public served installer remain a generated single-file artifact?
rationale: The request is useful maintainability work on a stable setup surface, but the current docs, workflow, tests, and release artifact assume one directly served script, so automation cannot choose the permanent artifact strategy safely.

options.title: Sponsor a guarded generated-artifact split
options.body: Approve an incremental source split only if it preserves one tested public installer file and updates website sync plus installer smoke proof in the same change.

options.title: Allow focused extractions only
options.body: Use this issue as backlog context and extract installer sections only when tied to concrete bug fixes or validation improvements.

options.title: Keep the installer monolithic
options.body: Decide that the served shell installer should stay single-file to avoid helper-loading and packaging risk.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a guarded generated-artifact split
recommendation.body: Approve an incremental source split only if it preserves one tested public installer file and updates website sync plus installer smoke proof in the same change.

likelyOwner.reason: Current installer blame, maintainer PR metadata, and package-manager installer history make this the strongest available owner signal for the source-vs-artifact decision.
